circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit, a 5. 281-kilometre track designed by Hermann Tilke on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, has been the venue for Formula One's season finale since 2009. The circuit represents the second of four Middle Eastern Formula One venues, following Bahrain's circuit and preceding those established in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: Albert Park Circuit is a street circuit located around Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, hosting the annual Formula One Australian Grand Prix along with supporting motorsport events. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification, meeting the highest international standards for motorsport facilities.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: The Red Bull Ring is a 4. 326 km circuit located in Spielberg, Austria, which originally operated as the Österreichring and staged the Austrian Grand Prix annually between 1970 and 1987. After undergoing modifications and a name change to the A1-Ring, the venue resumed hosting the Austrian Grand Prix from 1997 to 2003 before acquiring its current designation.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street track in Azerbaijan's capital situated along the city's boulevard, stretching 6. 003 km to rank among the longest venues on the Formula One calendar. First hosting the 2016 European Grand Prix, the circuit subsequently became home to the Azerbaijan Grand Prix beginning in 2017, with operations managed by Baku City Circuit Operation Company.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit is a 5. 412 km facility that hosted the Middle East's inaugural Formula One Grand Prix and continues to be a regular stop on the F1 calendar alongside other racing series. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 status and features multiple circuit configurations for various motorsport events including endurance racing.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a versatile layout combining extended straights with diverse corner configurations, making it suitable for testing various racing skills. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and can accommodate approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Spa-Francorchamps is a 7. 004 km Belgian circuit near the town of Spa that has been hosting Formula One racing since 1950, making it one of the sport's oldest venues. The track has continuously held the Belgian Grand Prix annually since 1985, with only two absences in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, Quebec, this 4. 361 km circuit serves as the home of Canada's Formula One Grand Prix. Beyond Formula One, the track has accommodated various international motorsport series including sports cars, open-wheel racing, and stock car competitions over its history.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: The Shanghai International Circuit in the Jiading District serves as China's primary Formula One venue, hosting the Chinese Grand Prix from 2004 to 2019 before resuming in 2024. The facility has expanded its motorsport calendar to include electric racing events alongside its traditional grand prix hosting.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located near Silverstone in Northamptonshire, England, this circuit has been the traditional home of the British Grand Prix since 1948 and hosted the inaugural World Championship race in 1950. After the event alternated between three venues from 1955 to 1986, it became a permanent fixture at this location from 1987 onwards, and currently also stages the British MotoGP round.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring near Budapest became the site of Formula One's first Eastern Bloc grand prix in 1986, built in just eight months near a major highway outside the city. Originally, plans called for a Monaco-style street circuit in Budapest's central park, but the government opted for a dedicated racing venue instead. The inaugural race honored János Drapál, Hungary's pioneering motorcycle racing champion.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: The Autodromo Nazionale Monza is a 5. 793 km Italian racing circuit constructed in 1922 near Milan, making it Europe's oldest purpose-built track after Brooklands and Indianapolis. Home to the Italian Grand Prix since 1949 (except during a 1980 closure for renovations), the venue earns its "Temple of Speed" nickname from its extended straights and fast-flowing corner design.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807-kilometer Japanese motorsport venue operated by Honda Mobilityland in Mie Prefecture, boasting a capacity of 155,000 spectators. The track has become iconic as a Formula One grand prix destination and host to the Super Formula championship series.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that navigates through Paradise, Nevada, tracing a path along famous sections of Las Vegas Boulevard where the city's premier resorts and entertainment venues are located. The layout passes by iconic landmarks such as MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas, creating a unique urban racing environment centered around the entertainment district.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the 4. 304 km Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is named after two fatal racing drivers, Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, who died in 1962 and 1971 respectively. The venue returned to hosting Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix from 2015 onwards after a 23-year absence, though it operated under different configurations during its earlier hosting periods that ended in 1992.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens that measures 3. 363 miles and incorporates 19 corners, allowing qualifying speeds averaging 139 mph. Designed specifically for Formula One by Apex Circuit Design, the venue joined the championship calendar in 2022.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3. 337 km street course that winds through the urban landscape of Monte Carlo and La Condamine, skirting the harbour area of the principality. The track is frequently known by the "Monte Carlo" name due to its primary location within that district.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes 35 kilometers west of Amsterdam, this 4. 259 km circuit hosted the Dutch Grand Prix after returning to Formula One in 2021 following a lengthy absence. The venue's involvement with the sport concluded in 2026, marking the end of its modern era as an F1 venue.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit sits north of Doha in Qatar and spans 5. 419 kilometers with a 1. 068-kilometer main straight.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Located in São Paulo, Brazil, Interlagos is a 4. 309 km counterclockwise racing circuit that opened in 1940. The venue was renamed in 1985 to commemorate José Carlos Pace, a Formula 1 driver who perished in an aircraft accident eight years earlier, and now serves as his burial site.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street racing venue located along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea waterfront that has hosted the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix annually since 2021. The track also accommodates international electric vehicle racing events.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's waterfront district, incorporating the Downtown Core and Kallang areas within its urban layout.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located near Barcelona in Spain, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya stretches 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced mix of straightaways and corners that test multiple aspects of driver skill. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and can accommodate over 140,000 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: Located near Austin, Texas, the Circuit of the Americas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility that annually hosts the Formula One United States Grand Prix alongside major motorcycle and endurance racing events. The track has established itself as a premier North American motorsport venue, having previously accommodated various racing series including IndyCar, rallycross, and sports car championships.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai and British racing driver who currently races for Williams in Formula One, competing under the Thai flag.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: The Spanish driver competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, having secured two world titles with Renault in 2005 and 2006 while accumulating 32 race victories over 23 seasons. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso achieved remarkable success in endurance competition, winning the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship and multiple prestigious sports car races including two Le Mans 24-hour victories with Toyota, making him the sole driver to claim both a Formula One championship and a World Endurance championship.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli races for Mercedes in Formula One, having secured six race victories following his entry to the championship in 2025.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman, a British racing driver, currently races for the Haas team in Formula One.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian racing driver Gabi Bortoleto competes in Formula One, currently driving for Audi in the championship.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas currently races for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from his 13 seasons in the sport. He achieved two consecutive runner-up finishes in the drivers' championship while with Mercedes during 2019 and 2020, and has accumulated 10 Grand Prix victories throughout his career.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto is an Argentine driver currently competing in Formula One for Alpine, bringing his racing talents to one of the grid's established teams.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Australian driver Jack Doohan combines reserve duties with Haas in Formula One, where he has started seven races since 2024, while also competing in European endurance racing with Nielsen Racing in the LMP2 category.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. The 2020 Italian Grand Prix victory with AlphaTauri stands as a notable achievement in his career.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar represents France in Formula One, competing for Red Bull Racing. The driver holds dual French and Algerian nationality.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British driver competing for Ferrari who has equalled Michael Schumacher's record of seven world championship titles. The driver holds multiple Formula One records including the most race victories, pole positions, and podium finishes in the sport's history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races for Audi in Formula One, bringing considerable experience from his extensive career in motorsport. Beyond his F1 commitments, Hülkenberg has achieved success in endurance racing, notably winning the prestigious 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 during his time with Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand motorsport competitor currently driving for Racing Bulls in Formula One.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc is a Monégasque driver competing for Ferrari in Formula One, having achieved runner-up status in the 2022 championship standings. Across his nine seasons in the sport, he has secured nine Grand Prix victories.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Danish driver Kevin Magnussen competed in Formula One across two separate periods, from 2014-2020 and again in 2022-2024, before transitioning to endurance racing. He currently races for BMW as a factory driver in the FIA World Endurance Championship with WRT, while also taking part-time NASCAR Cup Series duties with Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British driver competing for McLaren, secured the 2025 Formula One World Drivers' Championship with the team. He has accumulated 13 Grand Prix victories throughout his eight-season career in the sport.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Haas. He previously secured a Grand Prix victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix while driving for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio Pérez competes for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from a 15-season career that includes six race victories. He finished as championship runner-up in 2023 while driving for Red Bull Racing.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Australian driver Oscar Piastri currently races for McLaren in Formula One, having secured nine Grand Prix victories since joining the grid.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Australian driver Daniel Ricciardo competed in Formula One for 14 seasons between 2011 and 2024, securing eight Grand Prix victories during his career in the sport. Known by the nickname "the Honey Badger", Ricciardo has since retired from top-level racing.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell currently races for Mercedes in Formula One, where he has secured seven Grand Prix victories throughout his eight-year career in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz Vázquez de Castro currently races for Williams in Formula One, where he has accumulated four race victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver who raced in Formula One during 2023 and 2024 before transitioning to sportscars. He currently competes in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian Formula One driver currently racing for Aston Martin in the championship series.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda is a Japanese driver who has held reserve positions with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls throughout his Formula One career spanning from 2021 to 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: Competing for Red Bull Racing under the Dutch flag, Max Verstappen is a Dutch-Belgian driver who has claimed four consecutive world championship titles between 2021 and 2024. Across 12 seasons in the sport, he has accumulated 71 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu represents China in Formula One, where he currently holds a reserve driver position with Cadillac. The Beijing-born driver competed in the sport's top tier from 2022 through 2024, establishing a unique distinction as the sole Chinese national to have participated in Formula One racing.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based Alpine Formula One Team represents Renault's rebranded works operation since 2021, succeeding the Renault F1 Team identity. Operating with a French licence and powered by Mercedes engines, the squad has secured one victory in its Alpine era when Esteban Ocon triumphed at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix, with Pierre Gasly delivering the team's first pole position under its current name at the 2026 Italian Grand Prix.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin has been a recurring presence in Formula One through different organizational structures, with the current incarnation operating as AMR GP Limited under the Aston Martin Aramco branding.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of the Italian luxury automaker Ferrari, stands as Formula One's longest-running and most decorated team, participating in every World Championship from 1950 onward. Known colloquially as "the Prancing Horse" after their iconic emblem, the squad has established itself as the sport's most dominant force throughout its seven-decade history.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: An American Formula One outfit founded by NASCAR team proprietor Gene Haas, the team commenced racing in 2016 with a focus on competitive participation at the grid's mid-field level. Leadership transitioned in early 2024 when Ayao Komatsu assumed the principal role from Guenther Steiner, who had overseen operations since the team's establishment in 2014.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: Sauber was a Swiss racing outfit established in 1970 that progressed from building sports cars to developing Formula One machinery as an independent manufacturer. The organisation secured notable endurance racing achievements, including a Le Mans victory in 1989 with Mercedes-Benz, before competing in F1 from 1993 onwards through various ownership iterations until ceasing operations in 2025, at which point Audi acquired its assets to establish its own factory team.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing Limited is a British Formula One outfit headquartered at its Technology Centre in Woking, Surrey. Operating as a subsidiary of the McLaren Group under Mumtalakat Holding Company's ownership, the team competes in the sport's premier category.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has competed in Formula One since 1954 as both a constructor and engine supplier, with the current team based in Brackley and racing under a German licence. Following Ineos's acquisition of a one-third ownership stake in January 2022, Mercedes-AMG Petronas now operates with shared ownership between Mercedes-Benz Group, Toto Wolff, and Ineos. The team's tradition is symbolized by its "Silver Arrows" identity.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that entered the sport in 2024 as part of Red Bull's two-team structure alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with operations in Milton Keynes, the team operates as a second outfit under the Austrian conglomerate's ownership, functioning as a sister team within the Red Bull Formula One programme.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that began competing in 2024 as part of Red Bull GmbH's two-team operation alongside Red Bull Racing. Headquartered in Faenza with a secondary facility in Milton Keynes, the team operates as Red Bull's second constructor entry in the championship.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing competes in Formula One under an Austrian licence while operating from England as one of two teams owned by Red Bull GmbH. Since its establishment in 2005, the team was led by Christian Horner until his 2025 departure, with Laurent Mekies taking over as team principal.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering, established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head following the collapse of Williams's initial F1 venture, represents one of Formula One's prominent British constructors. Based in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team competes in the 2026 season as Atlassian Williams F1 Team and has maintained its presence as both a racing outfit and constructor throughout its history.
